newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's import car sales fall.
newsitem.headline: Japan's import car sales fall.

text.p: Imported car sales in Japan fell last month due to a rise in the sales tax but the pace of the slide slowed from previous months and showed signs of a recovery in the future.
The Japan Automobile Importers' Association said Friday that sales of imported vehicles fell 20.5 percent in June from a year earlier to 32,176 units, marking the third straight year-on-year decline.
Sales have been slow throughout the sector since Japan's sales tax was raised to 5 percent from 3 percent on April 1.
Domestic vehicle sales tumbled in April by 37 percent year-on-year and in May by 27 percent.

"June sales fell but the rate of the (year-on-year) fall shrank in June against April and May. That shows the undertone of the market is turning up," Ken Kano, the association's planning manager, told Reuters.
Imported car sales are expected to perk up in the autumn, when carmakers will launch a number of new models.
Japanese sales of imported vehicles in the first half of 1997 totalled 194,741 units, down 8.7 percent from the same period last year.
But sales of "genuine" foreign cars -- excluding those made by Japanese automakers overseas -- rose 1.6 percent from a year earlier to 166,932 in the January-June half year, Kano said.
Nobuaki Yanachi, senior analyst on the car industry at Kankaku Research, agreed with Kano that the market is turning up with the impact of the sales tax diminishing.
"Sales of imported cars may post gains (year-on-year) in or after July," he said. "Demand is still strong for Volkswagen, which is the best-selling imported brand in Japan, backed by Toyota.
Toyota's sales network handles about 60 percent of total Volkswagen sales in Japan.

The Volkswagen group, including Audi cars, topped the June list with 5,491 cars, up 10.4 percent from a year earlier, followed by BMW, with 3,554 cars including U.S.-made BMW Z3 models, down 10.7 percent, Mercedes-Benz with 3,262 cars, down 17.3 percent, Adam Opel with 2,892, down 31.8 percent and Rover with 2,860, down 0.8 percent.

Sales of Ford cars, including German-made Mondeos, fell nearly 60 percent in June to 910 cars, while Chrysler posted a 6.7 percent gain year-on-year to 1,506 cars in June and General Motors sales rose 20 percent to 2,035 cars.
"The Ford models were basically designed for American people not for the Japanese. Those do not match with Japanese tastes. They need to go back to a more conservative design," Kano said.
